title: Typed-response stream decoder smoke suite for token-level JSON enforcement and tool-call flows
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a focused smoke test suite that validates token-level JSON enforcement during streaming responses and across tool/function calling boundaries. This ticket covers integration tests that simulate partial-chunk JSON emission, mid-stream schema switches (via tool calls that return structured payloads), and graceful constrained-decoding fallback when latent unparsable fragments appear. The goal is a minimal set of deterministic scenarios that catch regressions introduced by recent decoder changes and streaming reassembly logic.
background: Recent runtime changes optimized streaming token batching and introduced a new decoder path for low-latency constrained decoding. Unit tests exist for decoder primitives, but we lack E2E coverage that exercises streaming + tool-calling interactions where structured JSON is produced, modified by tool outputs, and resumed by the model. Past incidents (INC-2025-09) showed silent schema drift in streaming responses when a fallback model was used mid-request; this suite should prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Create 6 deterministic smoke scenarios that run in CI (fast, <90s total): pure streaming JSON object, streaming JSON array of objects, mid-stream tool call that injects a typed object, partial-chunk broken JSON repaired by later tokens, constrained-decoder mode enforcement (rejecting unknown fields), and compatibility fallback that emits a minimal error object when schema cannot be satisfied.
All scenarios pass on runtime-1.24 and the new decoder-enabled runtime-1.25-beta in the compatibility matrix.
Tests produce machine-readable logs (newline-delimited JSON) with fields: scenario, model_variant, tokens_sent, tokens_received, parse_status, final_payload_sha256, and ci_run_id.
Baseline hashes recorded in test artifacts and a PR created to add these to infra-ci so regressions will fail the pipeline.
Documentation snippet added to the developer guide describing token-level recovery strategy and tool-call expectations.
Design/PM review completed and signoff captured in comments.
test_plan: Scenario A - Chunked-object: model streams a single JSON object in uneven token chunks; verify parser reassembly yields exact schema match.
Scenario B - Array-of-objects: model streams an array where each element is emitted after a tool call; assert ordering and types preserved.

Scenario C - Tool-inserted-typed: model emits a function call; the tool returns a typed JSON payload with extra optional fields; constrained-decoder mode must drop unknown optional fields or flag depending on policy.

Scenario D - Partial-break-and-repair: introduce a mid-stream token corruption (simulated by injecting an unexpected token), ensure decoder detects, requests a retry path, and final payload meets schema or returns explicit error object.

Scenario E - Fallback-compat: force a model fallback mid-request to a lower-capability variant; verify graceful degradation policy emits a compact fallback response document and an audit snippet explaining the fallback.
Scenario F - Streaming-to-sync handoff: stream starts, then a tool call completes synchronously and the model resumes; validate KV cache continuity and schema continuity across the handoff.

Matrix: run each scenario against model variants: small-fast, medium-quant, and large-compat; runtimes: runtime-1.24, runtime-1.25-beta; modes: constrained-decoder on/off; transport: chunked-http, websocket-streaming.
CI constraints: total suite must run within 90s using mocked network and short-sequence seeds; tests use deterministic RNG seeds and recorded response fixtures when applicable.
implementation_notes: Test harness will reuse existing streaming harness under infra/tests/streaming with a new adapter layer to simulate tool responses (see internal PR #2146).
Use NLJSON (newline-delimited JSON) for logs to simplify parsing in CI and to provide stable artifact comparisons.
Add a small shim to runtime test fixture to simulate token corruption and model fallback; this should be gated behind a test-only feature flag.
Coordinate with SDK team to expose a 'constrainedDecode=true' query flag in test endpoints to exercise the decoder path without modifying production routing.
Record final payload SHA256 to detect byte-level regressions rather than relying on textual diffs which are brittle across minor whitespace changes.
risks_and_mitigation: Flaky tests due to timing of token flushes: mitigate by forcing deterministic flush points in the harness and using short sequences.
False positives when downstream tools change schema: pin tool test fixtures and add explicit invariant checks rather than full schema equality where appropriate.
Runtime feature flags might drift from prod: keep the constrainedDecode flag test-only and add an integration gate to ensure runtime-1.24 behavior remains unchanged unless intentionally migrated.
Potential cost of running multiple model variants in CI: limit to three variants and use lightweight quantized images for medium and small models.
